quickref.name: Marecraft (Marecraft Arena / "The Marecraft")
quickref.era: Added in update 1.4.3 of the app then called "Battle Bears", which the wiki files under BBR. SkyVu said "April, 2013" [Canon]. The wiki dates 1.4.3 to Apr 15, 2013 and 1.4.3.1 to Apr 23, 2013 [Fan-wiki]. In BBG from its May 24, 2013 launch [Fan-wiki]. No documented removal or rework; BBG 3.0 (Nov 15, 2021) brought global "New Map Lighting" [Fan-wiki].
quickref.in_2026: Not named in the Steam store text [Canon]. Its track "Marecraft" (0:57) is on the official BBG Soundtrack (Nov 4, 2026) [Canon]. The Steam trailer shows it at 38.5–41.0 s, but that is reused 2013 footage [Inference, strong]. It appears in a 16-map grid on the official "BBG Maps Ranked part 1" Short, but the same grid is on a fan thumbnail [Observed]. Likely returning, not confirmed [Inference].
quickref.setting: Inside the digestive system of the Marecraft Carrier, the giant cream-yellow, blue-maned aircraft-carrier unicorn boss of Battle Bears: Zombies [Fan-wiki][Observed]. Huggable-style dark metal fortifications are built over living flesh, green digestive canals and intestine tunnels [Observed][Fan-wiki].
quickref.palette_and_lighting: Orange-red flesh #D34D3A/#DB5E39 (trailer grade #FF5026); deep tissue #9B342D; crimson organs #C24143; pale apricot ribs and ceiling column #E8A550–#F6A655; pink veins #DE7467; dark gunmetal #2A2520/#3E241D with lit deck #5B4744; navy ring portals #38415B; lime digestive canals #3C7E20 with #52B03B veins; teal tower light #69AEA5 [Observed]. Warm, even, enclosed interior light; no sky or daylight; flat, low-poly look [Observed].
quickref.landmarks: Central post-lined dark-metal bridge over four green digestive pools, with a lower cross-walkway beneath; two round sniper towers with satellite dishes and teal lights; a giant ring-segmented cream-gold column and apricot rib arches overhead, with dangling orange lobes; navy octagonal ring portals into intestine tunnels with jump pads; crimson tongue-like organ mounds, rows of pink-white gland nubs, pink veins draped over the metal; woven fibre mounds and a unicorn-pictogram plaque (the "stables") [Observed][Fan-wiki].
quickref.hazards_and_easter_eggs: Green digestive canals kill instantly and count as a suicide; gland ledges let fallen players climb out; underground jump pads lead up to each base [Fan-wiki]. Pickups: Bearscream Sandwich (bridge), Imperial Basket Grande and 2 Shields (cross-walkway under the bridge), 2 Health Packs (towers) [Fan-wiki]. Red and blue sockets on the bridge, possibly Plant the Bomb objectives [Inference]. Easter eggs: two outlines of a chewed-ear bear under the bridge, an early Botch/Assassin leak; the "two uvulas" trivia; a Mini Me ring glitch [Fan-wiki].

corrections.correction: | 38.5–41.0 s, Marecraft (inside the Marecraft Carrier: orange-red flesh, not lava) |
corrections.evidence: Trailer frames t_0078–t_0083 (38.5–41.0 s; full-res extracts at maps/dl/marecraft/trailer_hi/mc_38.5.png and mc_41.2.png) show vein-lined orange flesh walls, pale apricot rib columns, a round tower with a satellite dish and the dark post-lined bridge. These match the wiki's BBG icon File:Marecraft.png, the overview File:Marecraft_Arena.jpg and the official teaser thumbnails https://i.ytimg.com/vi/SSwlTVbW8Wg/maxresdefault.jpg.

corrections.current_text: (Steam screenshots and the Steam trailer; the lava caverns are from the trailer) ... there are lava/orange caverns and rocky caves
corrections.correction: The trailer's orange 'cavern' at 38.5–41.0 s is the Marecraft map's flesh interior (inside a giant unicorn), not lava. The only lava is Aztec Attack's lava pool in the aerial shots around 43–46 s. The whole Steam trailer is a re-edit of the May 30, 2013 BBG trailer, so it shows the 2013 look.
corrections.evidence: Trailer frames t_0078–t_0083 (Marecraft) versus t_0088 (Aztec temple with lava pool). The 2013 trailer thumbnail https://i.ytimg.com/vi/rfAyqVJrli4/maxres3.jpg matches the Steam trailer at 42.8 s (greyscale MSE 15.5, against 6,516 for an unrelated frame).

corrections.current_text: The wiki calls it the first intentional class leak [Fan-wiki] ([Marecraft (Map)](https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Marecraft_%28Map%29)).
corrections.correction: The wiki's Assassin (BBG) page calls it "the first known instance of a class being intentionally leaked in an Easter Egg" [Fan-wiki] ([Assassin (BBG)](https://battlebears.fandom.com/wiki/Assassin_%28BBG%29)); the Marecraft (Map) page only says it "was considered a hint to the character" [Fan-wiki].
